llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is best explained by a large DGD/PMD increase on a fibre span common to the affected working optical paths, likely in the shared S18–S19 underlay. The simultaneous roughly +64 to +65 DGD changes, BER increases, OTU_LOF/SD alarms, and protection switches fit DGD_RISE; unchanged optical power, OSNR, and amplifier telemetry argue against a cut, loss, amplifier, or connector fault.

proposals.rationale: Many independent receivers simultaneously show a very large DGD increase followed by BER degradation and OTU_LOF/SD, explaining svc218 and the broad correlated impact. The precise span is not isolated, although the shared S18–S19 spans—especially the aerial sections—are the strongest location candidates.

Mechanical polarization disturbance on a shared, possibly aerial span could affect many coherent channels at once. It is unlikely because SOP transients are normally millisecond events, whereas this case has a sustained large DGD displacement and continuing service loss.

Handling or movement of a common fibre could initiate a polarization-related event. However, this mode should produce brief power excursions, while the available channel, amplifier, and OCM power measurements show no corresponding change.

A filter shift can degrade quality without changing measured power and S08 is common to many impacted logical paths. It cannot readily explain the same approximately 65-unit DGD jump across numerous unrelated channels and receivers.
